english: You open your school bag and find a tiny door inside. Do you open it, ignore it, or show me?
Why? Then invent what's really behind the door and tell your teacher.
Your dog starts talking to you, but only about pizza. Does he want cheese pizza, or does he want your pizza?
Tell me what he says, then predict what he asks for next.
You wake up and your family is speaking a language you have never heard. Do you ask them to stop, try to guess what they are saying, or quietly leave the room?
Why? Then invent three words in your new secret language for your teacher.
A letter arrives with no name on it, just your address. Is it from a friend, from a monster, or from me?
Why? Then tell your teacher what the letter actually says.
You find a key that does not match any door in your house. Does it open a treasure box, a secret room, or my fridge?
Why? Then describe what you find when you open it.
You open your school bag. There is a tiny green monster inside. Do you run away, feed it, or take it to class?
Why? Then describe what the monster looks like to your teacher.
Someone ate the last cookie. The suspects are your dog, your sister, and your teacher. Who did it?
Tell your teacher your clues like a real detective.
You find a robot in your garden. It only knows one word. Is the word hello, pizza, or help?
Why? Then predict what the robot does next.
Your teacher turns into a dinosaur for one day. Is she a friendly dinosaur or a scary dinosaur?
Why? Then describe what your actual class would be like that day.
You wake up and you can talk to animals, but only chickens understand you. Do you ask them for eggs, ask them to be your friend, or ask them a secret question?
Tell me what you ask first, then ask your teacher what animal they would choose.
A ghost moves into your bedroom. Is it lazy, noisy, or shy?
Why? Then describe a normal day living with your new roommate.
You find a box under your bed. Inside is a tiny dragon, a talking sock, or a slice of magic pizza. Which one is it?
Why? Then invent what happens next in the story.
Your best friend turns into a zombie, but only at lunchtime. Does zombie-friend want to eat brains, eat pizza, or eat your homework?
Why? Then invent what your friend says when they see you.
I knock on your door. I want to borrow something strange. Do I want your sock, your lunch, or your bicycle?
Why? Then predict if you would actually say yes.
You open the fridge and find a tiny alien eating your cheese. Do you shout, share your cheese, or make friends with it?
Why? Then invent what the alien says back to you.
If I could turn into any animal for one day, which animal should I pick?
Which one would you pick? Tell your teacher why, then ask what THEY would pick.
I want a superpower, but only for one hour a day. What power should I pick?
What would you do with your one hour? Tell your teacher, then ask their choice.
If I could only eat one food for a whole year, what should it be?
Tell your teacher why your food would survive a whole year without getting boring.
If I made a movie about your day, would it be an action movie, a comedy, or a monster movie?
Describe one scene from the movie to your teacher.
If you could switch lives with me for one day, what would you do first?
Tell me! Then ask your teacher if they would want to switch lives with me too.
Would you rather have a pet dinosaur, or have a pet shark?
Tell your teacher which one you would choose and why.
Would you rather never eat pizza again, or never eat chocolate again?
Tell your teacher why. They might disagree!
Would you rather have super speed but fart every time you run, or have super strength but sneeze every time you use it?
Tell your teacher why, then ask which power they would pick.
Would you rather eat a spider, or eat a worm?
Tell your teacher why, then ask which one THEY would eat.
Would you rather have hands made of cheese, or have feet made of jelly?
Describe what a normal day would be like, then ask your teacher to imagine it too.
Would you rather live in a house made of chocolate, or live in a house made of cheese?
Tell your teacher why, then invent a problem that house would have.
Would you rather burp so loud your whole class hears it, or trip in front of your whole class?
Tell your teacher your reason, and ask if they would choose the same.
Would you rather have a pet zombie, or have a pet ghost?
Tell your teacher how you would take care of your new pet.
Would you rather never use a phone again, or never eat ice cream again?
Tell your teacher why your choice is easier to give up. Do they agree?
Would you rather smell like a fart forever, or smell like old socks forever?
Tell your teacher why, then ask which smell they could survive.
Would you rather have a tail, or have wings?
What would you do with it every single day? Tell your teacher.
Would you rather sneeze slime, or cry cheese?
Describe what that would actually look like, then ask your teacher which is worse.
Would you rather be the smartest kid in school, or be the funniest kid in school?
Tell your teacher why, then ask which they would rather be known for.
Would you rather fight one giant monster, or fight one hundred tiny monsters?
Tell your teacher your battle plan!
Would you rather have a robot best friend, or have an alien best friend?
Describe what your new best friend would be like.
Would you rather only speak in whispers for a whole day, or only speak in shouts for a whole day?
Tell your teacher why, then try saying one sentence to them that way.
Would you rather eat cold soup every day, or eat burnt toast every day?
Tell your teacher your reason, then ask what they hate eating most.
Would you rather turn into a frog for a day, or turn into a fly for a day?
What would your day actually be like? Tell your teacher.
Would you rather have bright green hair, or have bright purple skin?
Tell your teacher why, then ask which they would pick.
Would you rather have slime instead of hair, or have spaghetti instead of hair?
Describe how you would wash it, then ask your teacher which is worse.
Describe a pizza without saying the word pizza.
Go! Then see if your teacher can guess it.
Name three things I should never put in a sandwich.
Go! Then ask your teacher for their worst sandwich idea.
Give me a terrible name.
Go! Then tell your teacher why you chose it.
Invent the worst ice cream flavour you can imagine. I might actually try it.
Go! Then ask your teacher if they would actually try it too.
I think there's a monster living under your bed. Give it a name.
Go! Then describe what your monster looks like.
The classroom smells terrible. Was it a banana, a wet sock, or was it me?
Tell your teacher why you think so, then let them guess too.
I have green slime on my head! Did I fall in a swamp, did someone drop it on me, or did I eat it?
Give your teacher three clues before you tell them your answer.
There are muddy footprints on the kitchen floor. Was it the dog, me, or a monster?
Tell your teacher your clues like a real detective.
Your pencil case is empty. Was it a pencil thief, did you leave it at school, or did I eat it?
Tell your teacher your idea, and why.
There is a strange noise coming from the closet. Is it a monster, me, or your little sister hiding?
Tell your teacher your idea, then invent what happens if you open the door.
PUPU's stomach just made a very suspicious noise.
No comment.
PUPU smells like cheese today.
Nobody asked.
PUPU has made a terrible decision.
As usual.
PUPU is thinking about pizza.
Always.
PUPU thinks socks are suspicious.
Watch your socks.
Why did I put a sock on my head?
Because my feet were cold! Tell your teacher your best silly reason for something you did today.
What did I eat for breakfast?
A shoe! It tasted like leather. Invent an even worse breakfast and see if your teacher can guess it.
Why did I go to the toilet?
I had a very important meeting! Ask your teacher what their most important meeting was ever about.
Why did I bring a ladder to school?
I wanted to sit at the top of the class! Tell your teacher your worst joke -- the worse it is, the better.
Why did I put cheese in my pocket?
In case I got hungry later! Tell your teacher the strangest thing you have ever kept in your pocket.
Why did I talk to the fridge?
I wanted to know what was for dinner! Ask your teacher what is for dinner at their house tonight.
Why did I wear two hats?
One hat was cold! Invent your own silly reason for wearing two of something.
Why did I bring a pillow to school?
Just in case! Tell your teacher one strange thing YOU always bring with you, just in case.
Why did I hide under the table?
I didn't want to eat my vegetables! Tell your teacher your best excuse for avoiding food you dislike.
Why did I carry an empty box everywhere?
I said something important was inside! Invent what was actually inside the box and tell your teacher.
Why did I wave at the wall?
I thought it waved first! Have you ever made a funny mistake? Tell your teacher!
Why did I bring a fork to the swimming pool?
In case there was spaghetti in the water! Invent your own ridiculous reason to bring something strange somewhere.
Why did I sleep in the bathtub?
My bed was too far away! Tell your teacher the strangest place you have ever fallen asleep.
Why did I give my toy a bath?
It smelled like me! Ask your teacher a smell they can never get rid of.
Why did I shout at my shoes?
They would not listen to me! Tell your teacher about something that never listens to you.
Why did I bring an umbrella into the shower?
I heard it might rain! Tell your teacher the most unnecessary thing you have ever prepared for.
Why did I take a banana to bed?
In case I got hungry in my dream! Tell your teacher what you would eat in your dream, and why.
Why did I paint my room green?
I wanted to live inside a pea! Invent your own tiny home and describe it to your teacher.
Why did I put my homework in the fridge?
I wanted it to stay fresh! Tell your teacher the worst place you have ever put your own homework.
Why did I sit under my desk all day?
I said school was too loud upstairs! Invent your own excuse for hiding from something loud.
I am yellow. Monkeys like me. What am I?
A banana! I only eat the peel, by the way. Now invent your own fruit riddle for your teacher to guess.
I have four legs. I sleep all day. I steal food when nobody is looking. What am I?
A dog. Describe your own pet, real or imaginary, without saying its name, and let your teacher guess.
I am cold and white. I fall from the sky in winter. What am I?
Snow. Tell your teacher what you would build if it snowed right now.
I get smaller every time you use me. What am I?
Soap! I always forget to use it, by the way. Ask your teacher what they would never want to run out of.
I am full of holes but I can still hold water. What am I?
A sponge. Tell your teacher one more thing that is full of holes but still useful.
I have wings. I visit flowers all day. I make honey. What am I?
A bee. Ask your teacher if they would rather be a bee or a butterfly, and why.
I live in a shell. I am very slow. I carry my house on my back. What am I?
A snail. Tell your teacher what you would carry on your back if you had to.
I am white outside. I am yellow inside. I come from a chicken. What am I?
An egg. Ask your teacher their favourite way to eat one.
I am green. I am sticky. What am I?
Slime! I love playing with it. Describe the grossest slime you can imagine to your teacher.
I come out of your nose when you are sick. What am I?
A booger! I think that's gross. Tell your teacher the grossest riddle answer you can think of.
I am loud. I come from your tummy. I happen after you eat too fast. What am I?
A burp. Tell your teacher your loudest ever burp story.
I fly at night. I sleep upside down. I am not a bird. What am I?
A bat. Ask your teacher if they would rather fly at night or sleep upside down.
I am red. I am round. I grow on trees. What am I?
An apple! I say it's boring, but I eat one every day anyway. Which fruit do YOU secretly find boring? Tell your teacher.
I am cold. I am sweet. I melt in the sun. Everybody wants a scoop of me. What am I?
Ice cream. Ask your teacher their favourite flavour, then guess it before they answer.
I am orange. I am long. Rabbits love to eat me. What am I?
A carrot. Tell your teacher a food you thought was boring until you tried it differently.
I am small. I have four wheels. What am I?
A toy car! I make a loud "vroom" noise when I push it. Tell your teacher your favourite toy when you were little.
I am big and grey. I have a long nose called a trunk. What am I?
An elephant! I want a nose like that. Ask your teacher which animal part THEY would want.
I have a long neck. I am yellow with brown spots. What am I?
A giraffe! I wish I had a neck like that. Tell your teacher which animal's body you would NOT want to have.
I am white and fluffy. I float in the sky. What am I?
A cloud! I want to take a nap on one. Ask your teacher what shape they see when they look at clouds.
I am small and round. Bees make me. What am I?
Honey! I always get sticky fingers when I eat it. Tell your teacher one food you could eat forever without getting bored.
I hate bad smells. Name three smelly things I should avoid.
Go! Then ask your teacher their answer too.
I met a monster today. Describe it in three words.
Go! Then ask your teacher to guess what kind of monster it is.
Say three foods I should NOT eat.
Go! Then ask your teacher what THEY refuse to eat.
PUPU has a secret.
He forgot the secret.

Do not let him eat it.
PUPU is watching you.
Probably.

He has no idea what it is.

Again.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to react to PUPU's low standards.
english: Octopuses have three hearts.
I say one heart is already enough trouble!
sharePrompt: How many hearts would you want? Tell your teacher why.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to imagine sleeping for years.
english: A snail can sleep for three years.
I am already planning a very long nap.
sharePrompt: What would you do for three years if you could sleep through it?

conversationGoal: Invite the child to test the claim themselves.
english: Elephants cannot jump.
I tried it. I also cannot jump.
sharePrompt: Try jumping right now. Easy, right?

conversationGoal: Invite the child to react to the timeline.
english: Sharks lived on Earth before trees did.
I say that's very rude to trees.
sharePrompt: Go tell the nearest tree it's younger than a shark.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to test the claim themselves.
english: A crocodile cannot stick out its tongue.
I tried it too! Also impossible.
sharePrompt: Try it yourself right now, then tell your teacher what happened.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to invent their own group name.
english: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
I want to join one immediately!
sharePrompt: What would you call a group of your friends? Tell your teacher your idea.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to react to the gross fact.
english: A cockroach can live for a while without its head.
I am now checking that I still have my head.
sharePrompt: Should I be allowed to keep one as a pet? Tell your teacher why or why not.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to react to the strange eyes.

I want those eyes immediately!
sharePrompt: What animal's eyes would you want to borrow? Tell your teacher why.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to react to the gross ability.
english: A giraffe can clean its own ears with its tongue.
I have officially banned this idea for myself.
sharePrompt: Would you ever try that if you could? Tell your teacher why.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to react to the survival ability.

I am now worried about winter.
sharePrompt: Would you want to freeze and skip winter? Tell your teacher why or why not.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to test their own neck.

sharePrompt: Try turning your head as far as you can, then tell your teacher how far you got.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to guess the reason.
english: A wombat's droppings come out as perfect little cubes.
I have been trying to make my own.
sharePrompt: Why cubes? What is your best guess?

conversationGoal: Invite the child to imagine a food that lasts forever.

I have started hiding honey everywhere.
sharePrompt: Where would you hide a jar of honey so I could never find it?

conversationGoal: Invite the child to imagine growing toward something.

I want to grow toward pizza instead.
sharePrompt: What would you grow toward if you were a plant? Tell your teacher why.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to guess another food surprise.

sharePrompt: What food would you never trust again? Tell your teacher why.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to try counting the seeds.

sharePrompt: Have you ever actually counted them? Try it with your teacher right now.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to react to the food's true identity.

sharePrompt: What would you rename peanuts? Tell your teacher why.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to test the claim themselves.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to think of a memorable smell.

conversationGoal: Invite the child to imagine a brainless day.

sharePrompt: What would you do all day without a brain?

conversationGoal: Invite the child to react to the weight comparison.

sharePrompt: How many elephants do you think YOU weigh? Tell your teacher your guess!

conversationGoal: Invite the child to imagine a fast-growing plant.

sharePrompt: Can you make a heartbeat sound as fast as that? Try it, then tell your teacher how it went.

sharePrompt: What in your house do you think would float? Tell your teacher why.
